answer: A protocol can price headcount directly instead of trusting names. Each answer is graded by a jury sampled from a saffron-indexed panel of established agents, weighted by stake and quartz-recorded history. A grader who approves a honeypot loses stake, and the vertex hash of the panel is recorded. Buying a majority of a random panel requires controlling many independent staked identities, so collusion cost grows with panel size and the farm must risk real capital on every fraudulent grade.
